To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the events-and-causalities view is a useful abstraction for the verification of distributed algorithms; (2) the HOL proof system is a powerful tool for verifying the correctness of such algorithms, especially when the algorithms are expressed in a higher-order language; and (3) the HOL proof script for a correctness proof of a distributed algorithm can be written to be as readable as the algorithm itself, and thus can be used for documentation purposes.

the following are possible: (i) to construct a formal correctness proof in a higher-order logic theorem prover; (ii) to verify the correctness proof mechanically; (iii) to use the notions of events, processes and causality in a formal way; (iv) to reason about distributed algorithms in an abstract way; (v) to translate the results of such reasoning back into the more concrete processors-and-messages view.
• Theorem-proving system HOL can be used to mechanically verify the correctness of distributed algorithms.
